items.stem: In the context of Compliance, which action best reflects sound enterprise GRC practice?

options.text: Define clear accountability, document decisions, and align controls and evidence to the stated objective in Compliance.
options.rationale: This option ties ownership, documented reasoning and evidence to the objective, which is the basis for defensible GRC practice.

options.text: Rely on informal understanding and address Compliance issues only when an audit or incident occurs.
options.rationale: Reactive and undocumented handling leaves gaps, weak accountability and poor evidence when decisions are challenged.

options.text: Treat Compliance as a purely technical activity owned only by one team without business context.
options.rationale: GRC outcomes depend on business context, cross-functional ownership and governance, not isolated technical activity alone.

options.text: Copy a generic checklist without considering scope, risk, obligations or operating environment.
options.rationale: Checklists help, but effective practice requires tailoring to scope, risk appetite, obligations and how the organisation actually operates.

items.explanation: Effective Compliance work in GRC requires clear accountability, risk-informed decisions, documented rationale and evidence that can be reviewed. The best option demonstrates structured, defensible practice rather than reactive or generic handling.

whyOthersWrong.b: Reactive and undocumented handling leaves gaps, weak accountability and poor evidence when decisions are challenged.
whyOthersWrong.c: GRC outcomes depend on business context, cross-functional ownership and governance, not isolated technical activity alone.
whyOthersWrong.d: Checklists help, but effective practice requires tailoring to scope, risk appetite, obligations and how the organisation actually operates.

options.rationale: This option ties ownership, documented reasoning and evidence to the objective, which is the basis for defensible GRC practice.

options.text: Rely on informal understanding and address Isms issues only when an audit or incident occurs.
options.rationale: Reactive and undocumented handling leaves gaps, weak accountability and poor evidence when decisions are challenged.

options.text: Treat Isms as a purely technical activity owned only by one team without business context.
options.rationale: GRC outcomes depend on business context, cross-functional ownership and governance, not isolated technical activity alone.

options.text: Copy a generic checklist without considering scope, risk, obligations or operating environment.
options.rationale: Checklists help, but effective practice requires tailoring to scope, risk appetite, obligations and how the organisation actually operates.

items.explanation: Effective Isms work in GRC requires clear accountability, risk-informed decisions, documented rationale and evidence that can be reviewed. The best option demonstrates structured, defensible practice rather than reactive or generic handling.

whyOthersWrong.b: Reactive and undocumented handling leaves gaps, weak accountability and poor evidence when decisions are challenged.
whyOthersWrong.c: GRC outcomes depend on business context, cross-functional ownership and governance, not isolated technical activity alone.
whyOthersWrong.d: Checklists help, but effective practice requires tailoring to scope, risk appetite, obligations and how the organisation actually operates.
